To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 14-year-old patient with severe kyphosis from VATER/VACTERAL association was treated with posterior vertebral column osteotomy, circumferential fusion and instrumentation with a good clinical outcome at 2 years.

a 14-year-old with VATER/VACTERAL syndrome had a complex failure of vertebral segmentation and underwent a posterior-only vertebral resection with circum- ferential spinal fusion with satisfactory results.
severe rigid sagittal thoracolumbar deformity can be treated successfully with a posterior approach, vertebroplasty, and circumferentially fusing the spine.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to the development of a posterior-only surgical treatment of severe rigid sagittal imbalance, including kyphoscoplois, in a patient with a complex history of multiple prior spinal fusion procedures.
the analysis of the influence of the VATER/VACTERAL syndrome on the spine.
the development of a novel method for the analysis of the VATER/VACTERAL association.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the posterior-only approach for vertebral column resections is a valid option in the treatment of rigid deformity in patients with a history of prior spinal fusion.
a posterior-only vertebral osteotomy is an appropriate surgical treatment option in the setting of a failed anterior and posterior fusion for the treatment of a rigid sagittal deformities.
a posterior-only surgical technique, vertebrectomies, and circumferentional spinal fusion with instrumentation can provide a successful treatment for severe rigid sagittal spinal deformity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the posterior approach is an effective and safe alternative to anterior and posterior revision surgery for severe rigid sagittal imbalance.
posterior vertebral column ressection is an excellent option for patients with rigid spinal deformity, especially those with VACTERL/VATER syndrome.
a posterior-only approach with vertebral column resections is a viable option to treat severe rigid sagittal spinal deformities in the setting of a solid fusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a posterior-only approach can be used to treat severe sagittal imbalance in the setting of prior anterior and posterior fusion surgery.
a posterior-only surgical strategy can be effective for managing severe sagittal deformity associated with the VATER/VACTERAL syndrome.
posterior-only vertebral osteotomy and circumferential spine arthrodesis can effectively treat severe rigid sagittal spinal deformity, even in patients with prior anterior and posterior fusion.
